question: On the eve of independence, what was the GDP of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2.7 lakh crore**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's GDP **in 1947 was ₹2.7 lakh crore.**
 
• **some other economic facts about India on the eve of independence:**
 
• **Low growth**
 
 
• India's economy grew very little from 1900 to 1947, **with national income increasing by 0.4% per year and per capita income increasing by 0.1% per year. **
 
 
 
• **Low share of global GDP**
 
 
• India's GDP **was 16% of the global GDP in 1820, but by 1947 it had fallen to 4%. **
 
 
 
• **Agriculture-based economy**
 
 
• India's economy was 95% dependent on agriculture, and 85% of the population lived in villages. 
 
 
 
• **Poor economic condition**
 
 
• India's economy was in poor condition, with low employment rates, poverty, and a lack of opportunities. 
 
 
 
• **Exploitation**
 
 
• The British exploited India's economy, rural areas, manufacturing, and other sectors. 
 
 
 
• **Poor agricultural practices**
 
 
• The British did not use proper technologies, fertilizers, or irrigation equipment for agriculture. ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP of India****​**

 
 
• According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), here is some recent data on India's GDP: 
 
 
• 2024-25
 
 
• Nominal GDP is estimated to be ₹77.31 lakh crore, a 9.7% increase from Q1 of 2023-24. Real GVA is estimated to be ₹40.73 lakh crore, a 6.8% increase from 2023-24. 
 
• India's real GDP is projected to grow between 6.5–7%. The IMF has upgraded its GDP forecast to 7% for FY24-25. 
 
 
 
• 2023-24
 
 
• Real GDP is estimated to be ₹173.82 lakh crore, an 8.2% increase from 2022-23. Nominal GDP is estimated to be ₹295.36 lakh crore, a 9.6% increase from 2022-23. 
 
 
 
 
 
• The Central Statistics Office (CSO) releases six estimates of India's annual GDP over a period of two years and 10 months.
